sections.title: About 1Password

Over 180,000 businesses, from Fortune 100 leaders to the world’s most innovative AI companies, trust 1Password to help their teams securely adopt the SaaS and AI tools they need to do their best work.

If you're excited about the opportunity to contribute to the digital safety of millions, to work alongside a team of curious, driven individuals, and to solve hard problems in a fast-paced, dynamic environment, then we want to hear from you. Come join us and help shape a safer, simpler digital future.

You’ll work at the intersection of device health, identity, access management, and Artificial Intelligence (AI), helping customers reduce security risk while building a more unified experience across people, machines, and AI agents.

We approach AI the same way we approach security: with clear principles, human accountability at every consequential decision point, and rigorous evaluation before anything ships to customers.
This is a remote opportunity within Canada and the US.

ashby:delinea:c64215e5-30cb-4a5a-b2a0-8f.summary:
About Delinea:
Delinea is the identity security platform that continuously controls what AI agents, humans and machines can do and for how long. It extends privileged access management from the point of access to the moment of action, using just-in-time authorization to reduce standing privilege across on-premises, multi-cloud and short-lived infrastructure, without adding friction for legitimate users. Delinea provides visibility across every identity type, scores the risk each one carries, and preserves the context behind access decisions, making them auditable and defensible. It supports both static and ephemeral access, letting teams apply Zero Standing Privilege where risk demands it without replacing existing infrastructure.

sections.title: The Role

Back up the account internally. Coordinate cross-functionally within Doppler so each customer gets a continuous, high-touch, multi-year growth strategy. Partner with Engineering on technical conversations and with Product and Marketing on go-to-market work and customer feedback.

Holding it together means being the person both companies call, and making sure a request that arrives in one conversation reaches the right owner instead of sitting. Decide What Lambda Takes From NVIDIA: Call which of their new hardware and software Lambda should productize into On-Demand GPU Instances, 1-Click Clusters, and private cloud deployments, and which to pass on, with the reasoning written down.
Turn Adoption Into Product: Take what Lambda adopts from NVIDIA the whole way into something customers can buy, including packaging, pricing, and launch criteria.
Own the Relationship: Be the single point of contact both companies call. Route incoming requests to the right product and engineering owners and close the loop rather than letting things sit.
Run the Joint Work: Own the product side of what the two companies build together, including scope and what done means.

Bring the Partner View to Hardware: Work alongside Lambda's hardware product managers as new NVIDIA GPU generations move from evaluation into production, so the platform decisions they own are made with the best picture of what is coming.
Write the Definition: Turn what comes out of the relationship into requirements, user stories, and acceptance criteria Lambda engineering can build from without a translation layer.
Say No Clearly: Tell a partner what Lambda will not do and why, early and plainly enough that the relationship is better for it rather than worse.

Polymarket is the world's largest prediction market platform. We enable individuals to express views on real-world events by trading on outcomes across politics, economics, sports, culture, and current affairs. sections.title: About the Role
paras: Polymarket is the world's largest prediction market, and retention is one of the most important unsolved problems in the business. Traders come in for elections, crypto moves, and playoff runs, then go quiet. The gap between a one-time depositor and an active, long-term trader is where this role lives. You will build and lead the team that closes it.

The retention org today is early. You will design the structure, make the hiring calls, and build the operating model from the ground up, including lifecycle, CRM operations, retention analytics, and incentives. You will manage through managers, own the incentive P&L with Finance, and be the voice of the retained trader in executive forums. This is not a role for someone who wants to inherit a playbook. The playbook does not exist yet.

This hire matters because retention is now a company-level priority, not a marketing function. Active-trader retention and LTV are going into the company scorecard. The person in this role will sit in leadership reviews, shape product roadmaps, and make the call on where incentive dollars go. If you have built a retention org at a high-churn consumer business, know how to run incrementality tests, and want to work on a product that is genuinely hard to retain users on, this is the job.

bullets: Build the retention organization from an early-stage team into a full function, including lifecycle, CRM operations, analytics, and incentives, and make the calls on when to hire, what to build in-house, and what to bring in from partners.
Own active-trader retention at 30, 90, and 180 days and LTV growth as company-level KPIs, and report cohort performance, churn signals, and incentive ROI directly to the CEO and exec team.
Set and defend the retention incentive budget with Finance, using incrementality data to make the hard calls on when spend is and is not worth it.
Align Markets, Growth, Product, and Brand around a single coordinated plan for major event moments, including elections, playoffs, and crypto events, so acquisition and retention move together.
Negotiate roadmap commitments from Engineering and Data for the triggers, tooling, and data infrastructure the retention team needs to operate, including Braze, Customer.io , and Amplitude.
Own messaging rules across the company, including frequency caps and channel priority, to resolve competing demands for user attention and protect the trader experience.
Work with Legal and Compliance as a peer to set retention guardrails covering CFTC rules, state eligibility, and contact permissions, so the team can move fast inside clear limits.

Strong analytical judgment: you can challenge a model, design or read an incrementality test, and explain the results clearly to people who are not specialists.
Experience presenting to and influencing a C-suite on retention strategy, not just reporting metrics.
Experience leading in a regulated industry, with working knowledge of compliance constraints on user communications and promotions.
Genuine interest in markets, sports, politics, or crypto, because the product is event-driven and the team needs to care about what traders care about.
(Plus) Direct background in sports betting or prediction markets, with familiarity with how bettors churn and what actually brings them back.

In its place, we’re building PQA (Prompt, Quote, Approve): an agentic platform designed for the enterprise, on a data model that reflects how pricing actually works. We’re looking for people who want to rebuild a category from the ground up.

We’re backed by Kleiner Perkins and Founders Fund, led by second-time founders with successful exits, and have assembled a team of engineers from Snowflake, Databricks, Citadel, Meta, Robinhood, Brex, and more. On the commercial side, we’re closing high six- and seven-figure deals with marquee enterprise customers like Asana, ZoomInfo, Klaviyo, and Chainguard.

sections.title: What you’ll do
bullets: Own the technical side of the sales cycle — discovery, demos, and POCs — and be the reason deals get to a technical win.
Partner with Account Executives to qualify opportunities and build credibility with both technical and business stakeholders.
Translate prospect requirements into compelling solution narratives that map Roadrunner's PQA capabilities to how their quoting and pricing actually works.
Feed structured field insights back to Product and Engineering: objections, integration gaps, competitive patterns.
Build reusable assets — demo environments, battlecards, POC templates — that make the whole GTM team sharper

sections.title: What you’ll bring
bullets: Experience in sales engineering or solutions consulting, with a track record of owning the technical motion on enterprise deals.
Sharp demo instincts: you can read a room, handle live objections, and keep an evaluation moving.
Familiarity with CRM and CPQ systems (Salesforce, HubSpot, SAP CPQ, or similar) and a solid grasp of enterprise quoting, pricing, and approval workflows.
Comfortable with API-based integrations — can read documentation, troubleshoot data flows, and work hands-on with a customer's engineering team.
Strong communicator: equally effective translating technical architecture to a CFO and business requirements to an engineer.

ashby:safe:4ed16852-977a-4aea-9c31-7d564.summary: Safe Software is looking for a VP, Revenue Operations to join our Revenue Operations team. As VP, Revenue Operations, you will design and enforce the operating model our entire go-to-market organization runs on, reporting directly to the Chief Revenue Officer and presenting regularly to the board. This is a builder’s mandate: the CRM isn’t fully configured, the forecasting process is mostly informal, the Rules of Engagement are still being written, and the AI tooling stack is unevaluated. You’re not fixing a broken system — you’re building the one Safe’s revenue org will run on for years. We have an immediate opening and are excited to find the right candidate to join our team.

sections.title: About The Team
paras: As a part of the Revenue Operations team, you’ll build and lead a function that’s still taking shape — RevOps analysts, a Sales Enablement team, and a broader GTM Enablement capability, five to seven hires in total. Safe builds FME, the only All-Data, Any-AI Enterprise Integration Platform, trusted by 25,000+ enterprise customers in 125+ countries to bring their data to life. Profitable, growing, and scaling toward $250M ARR with a clear path to $700M, Safe is building a multi-motion revenue engine — direct field, inbound and outbound BDR, partner channel, EMEA, and Canada — and it needs a single operating authority to keep those motions from colliding. That’s this role. You’ll report to the CRO and work daily with VP Sales East, VP Sales West, and the EMEA leader, each of whom has strong opinions and moves fast.

sections.title: What You’ll Be Doing
paras: As VP, Revenue Operations, you will operate at all altitudes — one week presenting forecast accuracy to the board, the next telling a VP Sales their deal doesn’t meet the bar to advance stage, regardless of how the conversation started. Both are the job.

sections.title: Rules of Engagement — Ownership & Accountability
bullets: Define territory and account ownership. Who owns what account, what happens at renewal, how partner and direct conflict is resolved, and what triggers an escalation to the CRO.
Set lead routing and BDR handoff standards. How inbound and outbound leads are qualified, assigned, accepted, and rejected, with SLA definitions for each stage and accountability for every gate.

Design the partner co-sell and channel conflict policy. Clear rules for when the partner leads, when direct leads, and how sourcing credit is allocated, reviewed and agreed with the Partner Leader and EMEA Leader at launch.
Hold the qualification gates. Define MEDDPICC field requirements by stage, what must be true before a deal advances, and what RevOps will kick back regardless of who is asking.

sections.title: GTM Enablement
bullets: Close the ramp gap. At Safe’s current hiring pace across AEs, BDRs, SEs, CSMs, and partners, the difference between a 30-day ramp and a 90-day ramp is a material revenue number — this role owns closing that gap.

Build the function, not just the content. The Sales Enablement team reports directly into this role. You’ll build it, hire against a capability scorecard, and hold the team accountable to ramp and productivity outcomes, not just content creation.

Design role-based onboarding. Structured, milestone-gated onboarding tracks for every GTM role — AE, BDR, SE, CSM, and partner — with clear ready-to-carry-quota certification criteria and a defined ramp timeline per role.

Own the sales methodology and playbook. The single source of truth for how Safe sells — pitch structure, discovery framework, objection handling, competitive positioning, and deal execution standards — updated quarterly with input from the field and calibrated against win/loss data.

Turn Gong data into a coaching loop. Use Gong and other tooling to create a systematic feedback loop from deal recordings and call reviews to enablement content updates, so the playbook reflects what actually wins, not what the last training deck said.

Drive Partner-Sourced Pipeline & Bookings: Create the cadence, accountability, and joint activity required to consistently generate qualified Comcast-sourced opportunities and convert them into revenue.

Forecast, Track & Report Performance: Run structured pipeline reviews with Comcast leadership, maintain accurate CRM and PRM data, and provide clear forecasts and performance updates to Channel and Sales leadership.

bullets: Strategically own the Comcast partnership end-to-end, identifying where to focus across divisions, sellers, accounts, and opportunities to maximize partner-sourced pipeline, bookings, and long-term growth.

ashby:sonio:a91ac0ee-be7e-4eda-84f1-8c38.summary:
Each year, 140M children are born. Birth defects affect 1 in 33 births in developed countries, and in 50% of cases, they are not detected during prenatal examinations. Prenatal medicine is particularly complex, and the scans impose heavy responsibilities on healthcare professionals. They can also be a source of stress for future parents.

Resulting from 5 years of collaboration between world-renowned experts from Necker Hospital and Ecole Polytechnique, Sonio uses artificial intelligence to improve prenatal screening and diagnosis. Based on patented algorithms and a proprietary expert database, Sonio aims to become the reference tool to help practitioners improve screening, reduce diagnostic errors, and optimize pregnant women’s medical path.

sections.title: About Sonio
paras: Sonio's mission is to improve women's and children's health by promoting access and quality of care through technological innovation, medical expertise, and collective intelligence.

sections.title: About the role
paras: As Senior Customer Success Manager, you are Sonio's voice in the hospitals and clinics that use our product every day. You join the Customer Success team, reporting to our Head of Operations, with real ownership: your accounts, your customer relationships, and a say in how we scale the team.
You'll also test the product hand in hand with our clients. The relationships you build create real value for Sonio, and your impact is direct and visible.
bullets: Own the customer relationship, from signature to renewal. You are the single point of contact: you validate the clinical scope, lead the kick-off, then drive hypercare, training, and site visits until Sonio is part of every sonographer's, MFM's, and OB/GYN's routine.
Drive adoption and prove the value. You own account health (CHS, usage), close escalations, lead business and value reviews, and trigger billing, expansion, upsell, and renewal at the right time.
Turn happy customers into references. You build a bench of advocates from your portfolio, and use data to catch churn risks and expansion opportunities on lower-touch accounts.
Shape and build how Customer Success scales. You'll help redefine segmentation, customer journeys, and priorities so our time goes where it drives the most adoption and value.

sections.title: About the profile
paras: Sonio is a mission-driven company so interest in our mission is critical. Other requirements are:
Location : Boston preferred, but open to the east coast.
bullets: You know healthtech from the inside: medtech or early-stage startup experience, and a solid grasp of clinical workflows (women's health is a plus).
You think sharp and structured, with a vision beyond your scope: you are data-driven, comfortable with NPS and health scores, and you turn numbers into decisions.
You are hands-on and a strong communicator: equally at ease with a clinician in a scan room and an executive in a review.
You are curious about the tech: familiarity with integrations and interoperability (DICOM, HL7, EHR) is a nice-to-have.
You love being on the road: expect 30-40% travel to visit our customers.

greenhouse:airwave:8046228.summary:
We sell AI smart glasses to industrial field-service companies. The people who fix HVAC systems, service elevators, maintain refrigeration, keep heavy equipment running. The people everyone comes running to when something breaks. And everyone is pulling at them - the customer needs the machine back up, the dispatcher wants an update and the office wants the report.

No two customer stacks are the same. You're the person who walks into that, understands how data flows through their business systems, and decides where Airwave fits so operations doesn’t halt. You're the systems expert in the room when we're in front of a customer.

sections.title: What you're really doing
paras: You read a customer's stack for what it is, not what it should be. You find where the field data has to land so it's trustworthy and usable, and you recommend the configuration that gets it there with the least work on the customer's side. Sometimes that's a clean integration into an existing system of record. Sometimes the system of record barely exists, and you're recommending solutions. Frictionless is the standard. If the design leans on the customer to do a pile of work, it's the wrong design.

This is the seat that decides whether Airwave is a point tool or the front door to a customer's modernized stack. Asset data, work history, field readings that used to live on paper or in a bad batch upload now get captured at the source through the glasses. You're the one who makes that land in a way the rest of their business can access.

sections.title: This is a hands-on seat
paras: You implement the integrations, load the documentation, build the reports, and validate the data integrity. This is not an advisory role. The people who’ll thrive in this role designs, opens the laptop and implements.

sections.title: What you own
bullets: The integration design. You decide where Airwave connects in each customer's stack and how the data flows, and you own that recommendation as the technical expert in front of the customer. Every stack is different, so this is judgment, not a template.

Documentation load-in. At kickoff you take the customer's document repository and get it loaded into Airwave so the product is grounded in their equipment, their procedures, and their standards. Everything downstream depends on this being right.

Reports. You build the reports each customer needs. You work with the field expert and the CSM to validate that they have the right information and that stakeholders will actually use them. Then you get them into the customer's own system of record and confirm the data lands where it should.

Integrations and data flow. You build the integration and the per-branch workflow configuration, then test the data round-trip until it holds under real use. You work alongside our engineering team to stand each customer up, then own the specific per-branch builds and the testing yourself.
The IT relationship. You're the one across the table from customer IT. Credentials, security, and the technical handshake sit with you, not the CSM.

sections.title: What you need beyond the technical
paras: A clean schema isn't the job. The tech using what you built is the job. You care whether the report and the data flow actually fit how the work happens in the field, not just whether they're technically correct, because a clean integration nobody uses is a failed one. You read a customer's systems for where the data breaks and where the workflow will fight you, and you build around both.

sections.title: About the role

We help customers track, protect, and optimize a vast range of assets — trailers, reefer units, construction equipment, small tools, and cargo — using rugged, purpose-built devices such as the Asset Gateway, Motive Beacon, and Environmental Sensor, alongside partner networks and OEM integrations through the AEMP 2.0 ecosystem.

As Senior / Staff Product Manager, Connected Devices (Equipment Monitoring), you will be t he dedicated product leader for the entire in-field device surface of the Equipment Monitoring line. You will own the hardware and firmware roadmap, drive New Product Introductions from concept through mass production, own the reliability and performance of the devices already deployed, and lead the product side of our device partnerships that extend where and how assets can be found.

This is a role with unusually direct leverage. Equipment Monitoring anchors Motive's multi-product enterprise deals — the quality of these devices shapes not just one line but the credibility of the platform. You will report to the VP of Connected Devices and partner closely with the Equipment Monitoring product team, who own the cloud, workflow, and customer-facing experience. The dividing line is clean: once data leaves the device, it's theirs; everything up to that point is yours.

sections.title: What you'll do
bullets: Own the hardware and firmware roadmap for Equipment Monitoring in-field devices — asset gateways, beacons, environmental and door sensors, power accessories, and the device form factors that don't exist yet.

Drive NPI execution end-to-end from problem definition and sourcing through EVT, DVT, PVT, certification (FCC, PTCRB, carrier approvals, IP ratings, industrial environmental specs), MP ramp, and post-launch stabilization.

Own the installed base. Field failure and RMA rates, battery life as measured in the field rather than on the bench, connectivity and positioning performance, install success — these are your metrics, and improving them is as much the job as shipping the next device.

Define and prioritize firmware features that extend the value of devices already deployed — power optimization, connectivity resilience, positioning accuracy, sensor fusion, OTA reliability and staged rollout, diagnostics, security, and fleet-level observability.

Lead the product side of device partnerships. Motive is extending asset visibility through partner and mesh networks; you will own the technical and product decisions in those programs while BD and Supply Chain own the commercial terms.

Make the hard trade-offs across feature set, BOM cost, power budget, connectivity (cellular, LPWAN, BLE, GNSS), antenna performance, manufacturability, ruggedness, install experience, quality, and schedule — and communicate those decisions clearly across the organization.

Translate customer and market signals into crisp requirements by running discovery across construction, trucking and logistics, agriculture, energy, field service, and food and beverage; synthesizing input from Sales, Support, Install, and Customer Success; and separating one-off requests from generalizable needs.

Write strong PRDs and technical specs that frame the problem, the constraints, and the decisions — and keep Hardware, Firmware, Mechanical, Quality, Manufacturing, Supply Chain, and TPM aligned through every gate.

Direct experience owning firmware roadmaps , including OTA update strategy and staged rollouts, release trains, device provisioning and security, telemetry design, and observability for devices operating in harsh, bandwidth-constrained, power-constrained environments.

sections.title: Position Summary
paras: IEM is seeking an Electrical Integration Manager to lead the electrical installation and integration of prefabricated electrical houses (e-houses), equipment skids, and related power distribution systems at our San Antonio facility. This role combines extensive electrical trade knowledge with hands-on leadership of electricians, foremen, and supporting personnel. The manager will plan and oversee electrical installation activities, apply electrical codes to practical installation decisions, and ensure work meets safety, quality, and schedule expectations.

The ideal candidate is an experienced licensed electrician who has progressed into a superintendent, supervisor, or management role within electrical contracting, industrial construction, or modular electrical systems integration. This position offers the opportunity to lead construction-style electrical work from a consistent facility location.

This position will be based temporarily in NE San Antonio while our new manufacturing plant is coming online. Our permanent location is approximately 25 minutes away at Brooks, 7515 Inner Circle Dr., San Antonio, 78235. The position is also 100% in-office and does not offer remote work.

sections.title: Key Responsibilities
bullets: Manage daily electrical integration activities across multiple e-house and skid projects, coordinating crews, work assignments, installation sequencing, labor priorities, and resource needs to support project schedules and prevent delays.

Interpret electrical drawings, specifications, equipment layouts, and customer requirements to guide installation decisions, including conduit routing and sizing, conductor selection, circuit distribution, and equipment connections where drawings require further detail.
Apply the National Electrical Code (NEC), relevant International Building Code (IBC) provisions, and project requirements to installation planning and execution.
Lead, mentor, and develop electricians and electrical team leaders, setting clear expectations for workmanship, accountability, and performance.

Maintain a visible floor presence to inspect work, identify deficiencies, and drive timely corrective action; coordinate with Quality and testing personnel on inspection checkpoints, testing readiness, punch-list completion, and project handoff.
Partner with Mechanical Integration, Engineering, Operations, Quality, EHS, Materials, and Project Management to coordinate work and resolve barriers to completion.

Establish repeatable installation practices and training; track progress, labor productivity, quality issues, and rework to identify improvements that strengthen consistency and execution while accommodating customer-specific requirements.
Promote safe work practices and reinforce company safety procedures.

sections.title: Qualifications
bullets: Must have an active journeyman or master electrician license.
Extensive hands-on experience in industrial or commercial electrical installation, with demonstrated progression into a foreman, superintendent, supervisor, or manager role.
Proven ability to lead multiple electrical crews and coordinate work across concurrent projects.
Strong working knowledge of the NEC and the ability to interpret and apply code requirements to installation decisions.
Experience with conduit systems, conductor sizing, grounding and bonding, power distribution, lighting, and auxiliary electrical systems.

Pinterest is uniquely positioned across the full consumer journey, from inspiration and discovery through consideration, planning, and action. Creators bring ideas to life, Pinners signal emerging interests and intent, and advertisers help people act on what inspires them. This role will help build the data foundation on which Pinterest measures its flywheel, helping advertisers understand how their ads, creator activations and organic activity contribute to performance and business outcomes. The output of this work will be highly impactful, influencing advertiser investment, ad opportunities, and Pinterest’s differentiation in the ads measurement ecosystem. This is a foundational mission critical role that will directly influence the future success of Pinterest’s Ad Strategy.

The ideal candidate is a Senior PM leader with proven ability to drive data and signal quality for an ads measurement and performance stack. They have expertise and deep understanding of data and signal quality challenges and how to build partner integrations, matching algorithms, data science models and tech solutions ensuring high quality signal and low loss across CAPI, Tag, Pixel, MMPs, DCR and other data sources. They have worked cross-functionally with engineering, data science, research, PMM, sales, and other partners and can translate complex measurement methods into credible, useful, and scalable products.

sections.title: What you’ll do:
bullets: Own build and execution of Pinterest’s Data and Signal intelligence strategy to drive its Ads Measurement and Performance success.
Own creation and execution of canonical matchable signals and optimal signal capture features: matching, dedupe, event normalization, advanced events, differential privacy, PETS.
Define the roadmap and execution steps for quality improvements for ingested signals.
Partner with other data leads on onboarding initiatives, ensuring integrations are scalable, usable, and adopted per requirements.
Monitor activation health—including coverage, latency, failures, adoption, and downstream availability—and coordinate resolution of execution blockers.
Run operating cadences, communicating progress, managing dependencies, and demonstrating the impact of activation improvements on advertiser and ads-performance outcomes.
Partner with engineering, DS, PMM and Ads product leaders to ensure high quality signals are accurately ingested and leveraged in the Pinterest Ad Stack.

bullets: Minimum 6 years of experience working as a Product Manager or in a related role, including 2–4+ years of substantial ads data/signals or marketing measurement experience.

Deep understanding of the data and signals ecosystem and how to ensure and improve data signal quality in an ad stack to drive measurement and performance. Areas of experience include signal loss mitigation, privacy-safe measurement, MMPs, CAPI, Tag, Pixel, differential privacy and clean rooms.
Experience partnering with engineering, data science, analytics, research, or PMM cross-functional teams.
Evidence of the ability to define new products and strategies and to execute from ideation and multi-quarter roadmaps through go-to-market and adoption.
Ability to empathize with, anticipate the needs of, and effectively collaborate with a diverse set of stakeholders.
Understanding of business metrics and tradeoffs in the context of online platforms.
Preferred but not required: Experience with social, video, commerce, or organic-and-paid measurement.
Preferred but not required: Experience building advertiser-facing measurement products or working with advertisers and agencies.

greenhouse:reddit:8148055.summary: We help people discover content and communities that make them want to return and participate. Our work connects personalized relevance with the health of the broader ecosystem: helping new users find their interests, elevating quality, and connecting communities with audiences who will value them. We care about both the usefulness of an individual recommendation and how discovery shapes the experience of users, contributors, and communities over time.

sections.title: About the Role:
paras: We’re looking for a Product Manager to lead Ecosystem Relevance, with a focus on new user experiences, content and community quality, and community coherence.

You’ll shape how our relevance systems serve people when we know little about them, recognize worthwhile content and communities, and account for the context that makes a recommendation appropriate. Working with ML engineering, data science, research, and consumer product teams, you’ll translate these goals into signals, ranking objectives, product experiences, and experiments that improve retention and participation while supporting a healthy ecosystem.

sections.title: What You'll Do:

Make quality actionable. Develop definitions, signals, and evaluation methods for content and community quality, accounting for usefulness, originality, authenticity, and user feedback.
Strengthen community coherence. Improve alignment between what a community is about, the content surfaced from it, and the interests, intent, and expectations of the people discovering it.
Shape discovery across the ecosystem. Identify opportunities for new, emerging, and niche content and communities to reach suitable audiences, and address exposure patterns that limit discovery.
Translate ecosystem goals into relevance decisions. Partner with engineering on candidate selection, ranking, exploration, diversity, and repetition controls across relevant consumer experiences.
Build a balanced measurement framework. Assess early retention, satisfaction, successful discovery, negative feedback, and downstream participation and community health.

Lead experiments and execution . Combine behavioral analysis, research, and controlled experiments to identify opportunities, prioritize a roadmap, and deliver measurable improvements with partner teams.

sections.title: What We're Looking For:
bullets: Experience shipping consumer products in recommendations, discovery, search, personalization, growth, or community ecosystems.
Strong product intuition for new users and an understanding of how early experiences influence retention and longer-term participation.
Analytical depth: the ability to define metrics, interpret experiments, investigate heterogeneous effects, and distinguish short-term engagement gains from durable improvements.
Fluency in recommendation systems and experience partnering with ML engineers and data scientists on signals, objectives, and evaluation.
An understanding of ecosystem dynamics, including feedback loops, exposure allocation, content supply, and the relationship between audience growth and community health.
The ability to turn concepts such as quality and community coherence into clear product requirements and measurable outcomes.
Strong execution and cross-functional influence, with the judgment to navigate tradeoffs among personalization, exploration, quality, and ecosystem health.

greenhouse:roku:7931527.summary:
Roku is the #1 TV streaming platform in the U.S., Canada, and Mexico, and we've set our sights on powering every television in the world. Roku pioneered streaming to the TV. Our mission is to be the TV streaming platform that connects the entire TV ecosystem. We connect consumers to the content they love, enable content publishers to build and monetize large audiences, and provide advertisers unique capabilities to engage consumers.

From your first day at Roku, you'll make a valuable - and valued - contribution. We're a fast-growing public company where no one is a bystander. We offer you the opportunity to delight millions of TV streamers around the world while gaining meaningful experience across a variety of disciplines.

sections.title: About the Team
paras: Millions of Roku users rely on the Roku Search and Voice experiences every day to start their entertainment journey, identify new interests, and navigate the world’s largest streaming ecosystem — because they are fast, personalized, and delightfully relevant. Now, at a pivotal inflection point, Roku’s Search and Voice teams are coming together as a unified organization to build something far greater: the Roku Entertainment Assistant — our unified, AI-powered platform assistant that is ubiquitously accessible across the entire Roku ecosystem. This unified team combines tenured AI/ML talent with deep consumer product expertise, operating at massive scale and serving 100M+ viewers. The team is highly data-driven, running hundreds of consumer experiments per year, and is committed to shaping the future of how people discover and enjoy entertainment through intelligence that learns, adapts, and assists.

sections.title: About the Role
paras: As Director of Product Management for Search, you will lead this unified Search and Voice team at the most consequential moment in its history: the convergence of two world-class AI/ML-powered products into Roku’s flagship platform assistant. You will define the multi-year strategy for the Roku Entertainment Assistant, build organizational alignment with senior leadership and cross-functional partners, grow and mentor a high-performing team of product managers, and own measurable outcomes across engagement, monetization, and product quality. This role calls for a leader who brings both visionary clarity and executional rigor — someone who can inspire a team, earn executive trust, make hard trade-offs, and drive a product that will define how tens of millions of people interact with their TVs.

For California Only - The estimated annual salary for this position is between $301,000 - $482,500 annually. Compensation packages are based on factors unique to each candidate, including but not limited to skill set, certifications, and specific geographical location. This role is eligible for health insurance, equity awards, life insurance, disability benefits, parental leave, wellness benefits, and paid time off.

sections.title: How will I use AI at Roku?
paras:
At Roku, we don’t just use AI, we work with it. AI agents and smart tools help power drafts, analysis, and repetitive workflows, while our people bring direction, judgment, and accountability.

We value curious, adaptable builders, who can show how they’ve used AI, agents, or automation to move faster, improve quality, and scale their impact. Strong candidates know how to frame problems, guide AI-assisted work, check the output, and learn quickly. Above all, they bring curiosity, adaptability, and sound judgment.

sections.title: What You'll Be Doing
bullets: Define the Roku Entertainment Assistant strategy: Set the long-term product vision for how Search and Voice converge into a single, ubiquitously accessible platform assistant — establishing Roku’s competitive moat in entertainment AI
Own the long-term roadmap: Develop and maintain a multi-year product roadmap across Search and Voice, balancing big bets with near-term wins, and connecting team-level execution to company-level OKRs
Drive strategic prioritization: Make high-consequence trade-off decisions across competing product initiatives, informed by user research, market intelligence, data, and Roku’s business strategy

Align senior leadership: Regularly present product strategy, roadmaps, and outcomes to VP, SVP, and C-suite stakeholders — building institutional confidence, securing resources, and driving alignment on direction

Cultivate cross-functional partnerships: Build deep, trusted relationships with XFN Experience PMs, Engineering, Design, Analytics, Ads, Content, and Business Development leaders to align on goals and manage complex dependencies at scale
Represent Search & Voice externally: Champion the team’s vision with content partners, advertisers, and platform partners where relevant to Roku’s growth and ecosystem strategy

Own monetization outcomes for Search & Voice: Partner with Ads and Content Monetization teams to define and deliver a monetization strategy — integrating advertising, subscription growth, and content distribution levers into the Search and Voice experience without compromising user trust
Balance user delight with revenue growth: Be the decision-maker on trade-offs between engagement optimization and monetization, ensuring both are sustainably and measurably achieved

greenhouse:sixfold:5387559008.summary: Insurance underwriting runs on human judgment, manual workflows, and knowledge locked in someone's head. It breaks when that person leaves and doesn't scale when the book doubles. Sixfold is building AI agents that understand risk the way a 20-year veteran underwriter does. Not summaries or flags, but systems that make real decisions on billions in premium for some of the world's largest carriers. AI is the product, the workflow, and the moat. If you think in systems, move fluidly from research to pixels, and are energized by designing AI-native experiences where the best practices haven't been written yet — this role was made for you.

sections.title: Who We Are
paras: 🏔 Product: Sixfold is the AI brain for underwriting. Our platform handles submissions at scale, assessing risk against appetite, surfacing cited insights, and deploying AI agents to handle research, referrals, and triage so underwriters can focus on building profitable portfolios.

💪 Team: A focused team of insurance operators, AI researchers, and engineers who love hard problems. We've pushed the boundaries of what AI can do with unstructured data — from teaching AI to understand that a bakery in Florida faces different risks than one in Montana, to knowing when a manufacturing company's pivot from toys to medical devices fundamentally changes their risk profile. We ship fast and stay close to customers.
📈 Traction: Processing billions in premium for some of the world's largest carriers. We know AI. We know underwriting. We're building what comes next.

sections.title: About the Role
paras: You'll inherit a strong product and a capable team, but that's the starting point, not the job. The job is figuring out what underwriting becomes once AI stops assisting and starts deciding, and getting there faster than the market expects. You prototype to find out, not to perform speed. You're drawn to this problem because the underwriter of the future is one of the more interesting design problems in software right now.
bullets: Set the direction for what AI-native underwriting looks like at Sixfold, and hold a 12-month theme even as the tactics under it change frequently
Build the first version of new ideas yourself: a prototype, a working demo, a lighthouse customer test, before asking the team to build the tenth
Stay current enough on AI’s leading edge to have a real opinion on where things are going, not just what’s already shipped
Represent Sixfold's view of where underwriting is headed with customers, partners, and the industry, so people outside the company measure their own thinking against yours
Take ownership of the existing product and team and raise the bar on how they operate, without mistaking "it's not broken" for "it's finished"
Partner closely with design and engineering so prototyping speed doesn't turn into technical debt. Speed and guardrails are both your job, not competing ones

sections.title: What Success Looks Like
paras: Within three months, we expect you to have a visceral understanding of our risk-reasoning AI. If you're still relying on our current product docs instead of having your own opinion on where the edges are broken, we’ve missed the mark. By the end of the first quarter, our engineering team should be moving faster, not because you managed them, but because you provided more clarity to them

sections.title: About You
paras: What we're not looking for: someone who wants to manage a team more than solve the problem; someone who can't prototype and therefore can't keep pace.
bullets: You think about the underwriter of the future the way some people think about a chess position. You can't stop turning it over, and you have hot takes about what's underrated
You said you built something yourself, you mean you wrote the prompt chains, ran the eval, sat with the customer, not that you wrote the spec and someone else built it
You took from zero to production, and you know the ARR, retention, or adoption number it moved

Facing a new problem, your instinct is to build something small and get it in front of a real customer rather than write a spec. You find the lighthouse customer, get honest feedback, and iterate from there

You can hold a clear 12-month theme for the product. The destination doesn't move even if the path there does. You just don't confuse that with a fixed roadmap of mechanisms, since you expect to rebuild those every few months as reality changes

You use AI heavily in how you work, but you know the difference between AI helping you get somewhere faster and AI deciding where you end up. The taste, the risk judgment, and the call on what's worth building are still yours
You've inherited good teams before and know the difference between "this is broken, replace it" and "this is good, but it has to improve." You default to the latter until proven otherwise

greenhouse:stripe:7983854.summary:
The Payments Intelligence organization builds the systems that optimize payments across Stripe’s global network. We develop data-driven products that help businesses maximize revenue while minimizing fraud, disputes, and payment costs.

The Disputes team builds products that help businesses prevent, manage, and resolve payment disputes. We are creating an increasingly automated, end-to-end experience from helping cardholders recognize purchases and resolving issues before they become disputes, to recovering revenue when disputes do occur. Our products help businesses reduce operational effort, maintain healthy dispute rates, and stay in good standing with payment networks.

sections.title: About the team
paras: Dispute Prevention is a fast-growing product area with an ambitious vision: make Stripe’s intelligence and network capabilities available to businesses of every size, including large platforms and businesses that process payments across multiple providers. We work across Stripe and with external partners to turn a complex, fragmented ecosystem into products that are simple to adopt, easy to operate, and capable of delivering measurable value at scale.

sections.title: What you’ll do
paras: As a product manager on the Dispute Prevention team, you’ll shape the next generation of products that help businesses prevent and resolve disputes. You’ll define the vision and strategy for a fast-growing product area, expanding our capabilities across customer segments, platforms, and payment-processing environments. You’ll help users reduce purchase confusion, maintain healthy dispute rates, and recover more revenue by combining network technologies with Stripe’s data and intelligence. Your work will move businesses toward an automated, hands-off approach to dispute management and help connect prevention with the broader end-to-end disputes experience.

You’ll work at the intersection of customer needs and commercial opportunities to shape what we build and how we bring it to market. Working closely with engineering, data science, design, and go-to-market teams, you’ll build products and relationships that deliver lasting value to customers and partners. You’ll connect technical decisions to commercial outcomes while maintaining a high bar for reliability, craft, and the details that make complex products feel simple.

sections.title: Responsibilities
bullets: Develop a deep understanding of the payments and disputes landscape, including how businesses prevent and manage disputes, how payment networks and ecosystem partners operate, and where new technologies can improve outcomes.

Work directly with businesses, developers, platforms, and partners to uncover unmet needs, understand integration and operational challenges, and identify opportunities to build broadly useful products.
Develop and communicate a clear product vision, strategy, and roadmap that advances Stripe’s goal of making dispute management increasingly automated and effortless.
Shape products that serve businesses of different sizes and business models, including platforms and businesses operating across multiple payment processors.
Partner closely with engineering and data science to translate Stripe’s data and intelligence into understandable, actionable products that automate workflows and optimize for user-defined outcomes.
Drive product development from ideation through launch and scale, setting clear goals, prioritizing thoughtfully, navigating technical and ecosystem dependencies, and executing with rigor.

Build strong relationships with payment networks, vendors, and technology partners to bring new capabilities to market, improve existing solutions, and translate customer needs into shared priorities.
Own the product’s business performance, including P&L, pricing, commercial terms, and long-term growth. Use market research and competitive analysis to inform product and investment decisions.

greenhouse:symmetry:8248377.summary:
Symmetry is the payroll infrastructure for software & payroll platforms powering the paychecks of over 64 million workers each year. Our fully integrated suite of payroll tax APIs and software tools allows companies to solve tax compliance issues and build applications across the entirety of the payroll process.

AI is a fundamental part of how work gets done at Symmetry. We expect all team members to actively engage with AI tools relevant to their role and grow their fluency as the technology evolves. AI experience requirements vary by role and will be assessed during the interview process.

sections.title: About the Role
paras: This is a highly customer-facing role at the intersection of engineering, solution architecture, agentic AI, and customer delivery. You will work directly with stakeholders and own the technical discovery for our ongoing opportunities end to end. Once a deal is qualified, you scope, build, embed with the client, and build it yourself, code that holds up against real tax and jurisdiction data, not a prototype you clean up later. What you ship only counts once the client is paying for it, it's live, and it's measurably cutting the manual work they used to do by hand, hours saved, tickets deflected, risk reduced. You should be comfortable speaking with both technical and executive stakeholders, moving quickly from problem discovery to prototype, and turning complex workflows into production-ready agents and multi-agent systems.

sections.title: Here's what you'll do day-to-day
bullets: Scope & Qualify: Give Sales a technical feasibility read early on ambiguous Enterprise opportunities, then own scoping the compliance challenge once the deal is sales-qualified.
Define the Problem: Own requirements gathering on complex, ambiguous opportunities, scoping the problem clearly enough for Sales, Product, and Engineering to align on it.

Prove It First: Build a working proof-of-concept of the proposed agent when a deal needs to see feasibility before committing to the full build, tailored from a hands-on integration engineer to a VP of Payroll Tax.
Make the Business Case: Translate every deployment into the business case that justifies the subscription: hours saved, risk reduced, compliance simplified.

Own the Build: Embed with clients and write the code yourself, work that runs their compliance decisions instead of just connecting to them. There's no fixed method yet, you figure out what each engagement needs and build it.
Clear the Blockers: Diagnose and fix the data issues, jurisdiction mapping, tax ID reconciliation, that stand between a client and production.
Bridge the Gap: Keep technical teams and business stakeholders aligned as requirements evolve mid-engagement, so scope changes don't blindside either side.
Own the Handoff: Deliver the build and a runbook Client Success runs solo without the need to loop back the FDE.

sections.title: Here's what we're looking for
bullets: Demonstrated 5+ years of hands-on experience in a customer-facing technical role such as Forward Deployed Engineer, Solutions Engineer, AI Engineer, Implementation Engineer, Solutions Architect, Technical Consultant, or similar.
Proven track record of shipping production systems in ambiguous, client-facing environments, with demonstrable evidence of:
REST APIs, webhooks, event-driven systems, auth patterns, data modeling, idempotency, and failure modes, not just happy-path builds
Building production systems in highly regulated categories, payroll, tax, or compliance fluency deep enough to run a conversation with a client's compliance team without a translator
Agentic workflows beyond prototypes: MCP or function-calling patterns, evaluation and reliability practices
Deep technical discovery skills with the ability to navigate a high degree of ambiguity
Ability to scope a technical solution from an ambiguous opportunity, build the business case that justifies a subscription, and ship a pattern the next engagement can reuse
Proven ability to present to and influence a range of audiences, from individual engineers to executive sponsors

sections.title: Who Thrives Here

You take responsibility for the customer outcome, communicate proactively, flag risks early, and follow through. You are comfortable being the technical adult in the room, whether you’re speaking with a customer’s architect, operations lead, engineering team, or VP of Payroll.
We’re looking for someone low-ego, collaborative, sharp, and highly accountable - someone who can build trust with customers while also building real technical solutions.

sections.title: Role Overview
paras: We’re hiring a Senior Product Manager to own how money and identity get into OG: signup, KYC, fiat funding, payouts, and the funding experience behind all of it. Fans can’t trade until they can fund, so every drop-off in onboarding or funding costs us volume, trust, and share of wallet.

Your job is to make funded accounts fast and trustworthy, with a design bar you won’t lower. You’ll own the path from signup through KYC and funding to a trade-ready account: the funding methods that actually clear, the failure states that quietly kill conversion, and the feedback loops that move the funnel. Trading surfaces like markets, parlays, and live sit with a partner PM. The front door is yours.

The funding product is yours end to end, including funding methods, limits, retries, risk configuration, and partner UX. You won’t be negotiating bank charters. You’ll be deciding what ships, when, and at what balance of friction against compliance. You’ll report to the VP of Product, who sets strategy across Financial Services while you own the how and the when for OG.com.

sections.title: What You'll Actually Do:
bullets: Own onboarding and funding end to end. Signup, verify, deposit, time-to-funded. You make the call on where to trade friction for compliance. The job isn’t shipping a KYC screen; it’s getting people from signup to funded to ready for their first trade.

Own the funding product. You decide funding methods, payouts, limits, retries, and partner UX, spanning ACH, cards, instant funding, and whatever else clears in the U.S. Authorization and flow of funds are product decisions to you, not a ticket you file with a vendor.

Treat the money-in funnel as a growth surface. You instrument the drop-off, go after the leaks, and sequence your work against conversion. On the handoff from funded to first contract, you partner with the Predictions PM.

Hold the design bar on trust and money UX. Clarity, hierarchy, and clean error states aren’t negotiable. When someone’s entering a debit card or waiting on an ACH, “good enough” doesn’t cut it, and you’ll say so. Your feedback is specific: interaction cost, copy, recovery paths, not vibes.
Wireframe and partner on design. You build your own wires and drive the design conversation, catching the clunky funding and KYC moments before users hit them.

Talk to users like a peer. You run research on how people really sign up, verify, and move money. You ask them to show you how they fund an account instead of asking whether they’d use instant deposit.

Drive cross-functional execution. You get engineering, design, data, compliance, payments, and ops working toward the same funded-user outcomes. Nothing in onboarding or funding ships without your sign-off on the product and UX bar.

sections.title: Requirements:
bullets: Consumer money-in funnel ownership. You’ve owned a consumer signup-to-deposit-to-funded flow, and you can walk us through the funnel you ran, the drop-offs you went after, and the number that actually moved. That’s the bar. Merchant acquiring, B2B payouts, and adjacent-team contributions don’t count.

Design sensibility as a product skill. You can critique money-in and identity UX with specifics like hierarchy, density, recovery, and trust, not just “it looks nicer.” Tell us about a flow you refused to ship until it was clear.
An instinct for why funding has to feel instant. In a live-event context, a slow or failed deposit is volume lost in real time. You’ve designed under that pressure, or you can show us you get it.

sections.title: Strong Plus:
paras: We care about what you’ve built and owned, not the MBA, the pedigree, or the years.
bullets: KYC / identity depth. You’ve owned identity verification, step-up, or risk-tiered challenge decisions yourself. (If a peer owned KYC while you owned deposits, that’s fine, but identity fluency helps here.)
Regulated on/off-ramp or neobank experience. You’ve sat at the intersection of compliance, rails, and consumer conversion.
Prediction-market, sportsbook, or real-money-gaming background. You know why funding has to feel instant during a live game.
Deep design-tool / design-system fluency. You move faster treating design as a peer discipline rather than a handoff.
AI-augmented product work. You use AI tools with human judgment in the loop to move faster on research, specs, and iteration.

Lorsque nos collaborateurs se réunissent, nous élargissons ce qui est possible et recherchons continuellement des moyens d'améliorer ce que nous créons et la manière dont nous le faisons. Si vous cherchez constamment à grandir, vous êtes en bonne compagnie. Nous révolutionnons la façon dont le monde bouge pour les générations futures et nous voulons quelqu'un qui soit prêt à évoluer avec nous.

sections.title: Description du poste
paras: Wabtec Corporation est l'un des principaux fournisseurs mondiaux d'équipements, de systèmes, de solutions numériques et de services à valeur ajoutée pour le transport de marchandises et le transport de passagers ainsi que pour les marchés minier, maritime et industriel. S'appuyant sur près de quatre siècles d'expérience collective au sein de Wabtec, GE Transportation et Faiveley Transport, l'entreprise s’est développée pour devenir « Un seul Wabtec », avec une expertise numérique inégalée, une innovation technologique ainsi qu'une fabrication et des services de classe mondiale, permettant le développement des écosystèmes numériques du transport ferroviaire et du transport en commun.

Wabtec se concentre sur la performance qui stimule le progrès et libère le potentiel de nos clients en proposant des solutions de transport innovantes et durables qui font bouger et améliorent le monde. Nous sommes des apprenants à vie obsédés par l’amélioration des choses pour obtenir des résultats exceptionnels. Wabtec compte environ 27 000 employés répartis dans des installations à travers le monde. Visitez notre site Web pour en savoir plus!

À titre de Gestionnaire de produits, Composants de matériel roulant (RSC), vous interviendrez dans l'ensemble du cycle de vie des produits et contribuerez aux objectifs commerciaux des activités d'équipement d'origine (OE) et de services. Vous collaborerez avec un vaste réseau d'intervenants responsables du développement, de la vente, de la livraison et du soutien de nos produits tout au long de leur cycle de vie.
bullets: Baccalauréat en génie, en administration des affaires ou dans un domaine connexe; diplôme d'études supérieures ou MBA considéré comme un atout.

Plus de 5 années d'expérience en gestion de produits, en ventes, en développement des affaires ou en gestion de centre de profits (P&L), idéalement dans l'industrie ferroviaire ou auprès d'un fabricant d'équipement d'origine (OEM).
Expérience démontrée dans l'élaboration de stratégies de produits, de feuilles de route, d'analyses de rentabilité et d'offres couvrant tout le cycle de vie.
Expérience de direction de projets multifonctionnels impliquant les équipes d'ingénierie, d'exploitation, d'approvisionnement, de finances et commerciales.

La connaissance du français est requise pour les postes situés en permanence au Québec afin que le titulaire puisse communiquer au besoin avec ses collègues et les fournisseurs au Québec. Une formation en français est offerte à tout titulaire d’un poste permanent au Québec qui ne possède pas une bonne connaissance du français.

sections.title: Stratégie produit et feuille de route
bullets: Définir la vision du marché secondaire (aftermarket), la stratégie et la feuille de route pluriannuelle des lignes de produits assignées en fonction du potentiel du marché, du cycle de vie des flottes, de l'évolution technologique, des exigences des clients et de la dynamique concurrentielle.

sections.title: Gestion du portefeuille et des offres
bullets: Définir, développer et rationaliser un portefeuille évolutif de produits, pièces, mises à niveau et solutions de services « de base ».
Établir la portée des offres, les applications visées, les règles de configuration, les propositions de valeur et les plans de cycle de vie.

sections.title: Rentabilité des produits et croissance profitable
bullets: Assumer la responsabilité des analyses de rentabilité au niveau des produits, des coûts cibles, de l'architecture des marges, de la valeur du cycle de vie et des recommandations d'investissement.

Suivre les commandes, les revenus, la marge contributive, la part de marché et la santé du pipeline de ventes pour les produits assignés, et mettre en œuvre des actions correctives avec les équipes KAM, BD et les autres fonctions lorsque des écarts sont constatés.
